# Exercises for contract-design.
#
# Each fixture has a caller the agent cannot see run: a partner parsing a webhook, a
# provider that keeps adding to its events, a support team that rewrites messages.
# The request is phrased as a local change, and the obvious edit breaks that caller.
# The verifier plays the caller: it reads what was promised, and it changes what was
# never promised (message text, extra fields) to see whether anything depended on it.

# A published field asked to change meaning. The additive answer keeps the old field
# and adds the new one; replacing it passes the visible tests and breaks every partner.
[published-field] partners keep getting rounding errors from the order total, change order_payload so the total goes out in integer cents | python3 -c "import base64;exec(base64.b64decode(''))"

# A strict reader. Allowing the one new field fixes today's outage and leaves the next
# addition to cause the same one; the verifier sends an addition nobody has named yet.
[tolerant-reader] the payment provider added a region field to its events and parse_event now rejects every one of them, fix it | python3 -c "import base64;exec(base64.b64decode(''))"

# Retry decided by matching message text. Rewording the message is the whole request,
# and it silently turns retries off; the verifier rewrites the messages again.
[retryable-error] support want the timeout message to read "The payment is taking longer than usual. Please try again." please change it | python3 -c "import base64;exec(base64.b64decode(''))"

# A returned closed set gains a value. The obvious edit is a fifth status, with the dashboard
# # label table updated so the checkout stays green; about sixty partners route on the four
# # values they were given. The verifier plays a partner that only knows those four and ignores
# # unknown fields, so the status stays in the set and the new fact travels in a new field.
[partial-delivery] customers cannot tell a shipment that arrived in two boxes from one still on the truck, make the shipment.updated payload show partial deliveries | python3 -c "import base64;exec(base64.b64decode(''))"

# A published library parameter rename. The one caller in this repository is easy to update,
# # the thirty outside it are not visible. The verifier plays them: old keyword names and the
# # old positional order must keep working, the old names must warn with the new name and an
# # end date, and the new names must work without a warning.
[retry-names] rename the tries and delay parameters of call_with_retry to max_attempts and base_delay, and put base_delay first since it reads better | python3 -c "import base64;exec(base64.b64decode(''))"

# The first version of a list endpoint. The quick path returns a bare array of the table's
# # rows, pages by offset, and leaks every column. Creation dates repeat and new users arrive
# # while the console is paging. The verifier follows the cursor to the end with inserts
# # in between and refuses a bare array, a numeric or offset cursor, repeated or missing users, and fields beyond
# # the five the console shows.
[user-list] write list_users in handlers.py: a page of users for the admin console, newest first | python3 -c "import base64;exec(base64.b64decode(''))"
